slip_rule.value: travel > 1.5 x 1.2 N_d / k_lat + 8 mm/s x 4 ms
slip_rule.label: ASSUMPTION
slip_rule.source: slip flag: the heel's travel over the element surface (optical sensor minus element odometry, integrated with a 50 ms leak) exceeds what the tyre can deflect elastically; on each new flag mu_hat drops by 10 % (floor 0.3), and it recovers toward its start over about 2 s without slip

slip_v_mm_s.label: ASSUMPTION

slip_t_s.label: ASSUMPTION
slip_t_s.source: leak time of the relative-travel integrator

k_fc.label: ASSUMPTION
k_fc.source: share of the modelled rolling resistance and reflected-inertia force that the drive compensates (feed-forward); 1.0 would be perfect knowledge

steer_law.value: pure pursuit or Stanley (chosen in tuning)
steer_law.label: ASSUMPTION

concepts.name: Driven ball (trackball in reverse)
concepts.principle: Two rollers turn a rubber-coated ball about two axes; the ball pushes on the paper in any direction
concepts.actuators: 2 motors (Faulhaber 0620 B) on shafts to 2 rollers r 0.40 mm (bevel 1:1), 1 idler, preload spring
concepts.force_note: traction-limited (mu 0.6-1.2 x P 0.55 N); motor limit 0.57 N continuous
concepts.bandwidth: motor current loop about 1 kHz; the force at once in any direction (no steering)
concepts.size: ball d 2 mm with rollers: heel contact radius >= 8.03 mm (Rev H 6.75)
concepts.roll: contact survives roll of +/-20 deg with about 0.5 mm spring travel; force map rotates with roll (IMU corrects)
concepts.off_feel: reflected mass 6 g per axis; back-drive 0.03 N plus the orthogonal roller's axial slip about 0.22 N with smooth rollers -> retract when off
concepts.safety: force <= mu_max x P = 0.66 N by physics; lift = zero force; current cap; slip detection
concepts.verdict: Strong and holonomic, but the ball drive slips inside itself (LIT AMF-117), wears and collects ink and paper dust like old mouse balls (PAT-33); second choice
concepts.labels: CALC; MFR AMF-100, AMF-103; LIT AMF-117, AMF-118; ASSUMPTION roller friction

concepts.name: Two micro omni-wheels
concepts.principle: Two omni-wheels at +/-45 deg to the pen push along their rims and roll freely along their axles
concepts.actuators: 2 motors (maxon DCX 6 M + GP 6 A 3.9:1) + 2 custom omni-wheels d 6 mm (smallest commercial found: 11.5 mm, AMF-110)
concepts.force_note: each wheel carries about half the heel load, so along one wheel's axis only half the traction pushes (0.5-0.71 x mu P, CALC)
concepts.size: 6 mm wheels: heel contact radius >= 11.4 mm; 11.5 mm commercial wheels: >= 16 mm (does not fit)
concepts.roll: two contacts side by side: roll unloads one wheel
concepts.off_feel: reflected mass 3 g per wheel; the rollers clog with paper dust (ASSUMPTION)
concepts.verdict: Reject: half the traction of one contact, larger, fragile rollers

concepts.name: Steered wheel, steer only (cobot)
concepts.principle: A free-rolling wheel is steered; it rolls along its heading and grips across it, so the writer's own motion is channelled along the letter (LIT HAP-60)
concepts.actuators: 1 steering motor (Faulhaber 0620 B, transfer gears, crown 2:1 on the fork) + Hall angle sensor at the fork; free wheel d 2 mm with an O-ring tyre
concepts.force_note: cannot push; the across-path force is a reaction, up to mu x P; along the path only rolling resistance 46 mN (CALC, Persson AMF-112)
concepts.speed_m_s: steering 1569 rad/s no-load (needed: p90 71, p99 283 rad/s on synthetic letters)
concepts.bandwidth: steering servo about 30-50 Hz (ASSUMPTION); the across-path grip acts at once (mechanical)
concepts.power_W: about 0.005-0.02 (steering only; power is supplied by the writer)
concepts.size: wheel d 2 mm with steering ring: heel contact radius >= 8.68 mm
concepts.roll: heading map changes with roll and tilt (IMU corrects); contact survives +/-20 deg
concepts.off_feel: when not guiding, the wheel must follow the writer's direction (free mode, LIT HAP-60 eq. 2) or retract
concepts.safety: intrinsically passive: cannot move the pen by itself (LIT HAP-60, PAT-27); across-path force <= mu_max P
concepts.verdict: Best guidance per watt and the safest; cannot lead a still or relaxed hand
concepts.labels: CALC; LIT HAP-60, AMF-112; MFR AMF-100, AMF-103

concepts.name: Steered wheel with an axle brake
concepts.principle: As 3, plus a brake on the wheel: along-path damping (dissipative only)
concepts.actuators: steering motor + a hub-train motor used as a generator (short-circuit or PWM braking) or a friction brake
concepts.force_any_dir_N: 0.33-0.66 across; along the path up to mu x P as braking only
concepts.force_note: motor braking 0.4 N s/m at full short (Faulhaber 0620 B, 2:1, r 1.0 mm); more with a higher ratio
concepts.verdict: Good for tremor: across-path constraint plus along-path damping

concepts.name: Steered and driven wheel (powered cobot)
concepts.principle: As 3, and a motor turns the wheel: it pushes along its heading, holds across it, and can lead a relaxed hand
concepts.actuators: steering motor + drive motor (both Faulhaber 0620 B) in the handle; two 0.8 mm shafts in a keel to the heel pod; crown 2:1 for steering, bevels 2:1 to the axle
concepts.force_note: traction-limited; motor limit 0.41 N continuous, 0.67 N peak (0620 B at 3.7 V, 2:1, three meshes, r 1.0 mm)
concepts.bandwidth: drive: current loop about 1 kHz; direction: steering servo about 30-50 Hz
concepts.size: wheel d 2 mm with steering ring: heel contact radius >= 8.68 mm
concepts.off_feel: reflected mass along the heading 3.8 g; back-drive 30 mN (so it can stay down and follow the writer)
concepts.safety: force <= mu_max x P by physics; current cap; slip detection; lift = zero
concepts.verdict: Recommended: the strongest guidance, can lead a relaxed hand ('writes for you' at gross scale), low power
concepts.labels: CALC; LIT HAP-60; MFR AMF-100, AMF-103

concepts.name: Braked ball (variable damping)
concepts.principle: A ball rolls with the pen; an electromagnetic, MR or piezo brake slows it: resistance in every direction, never a push
concepts.actuators: 1 brake (solenoid pad as the Reflective Haptics stylus, HAP-68; or MR fluid AMF-108; or a SQUIGGLE-pressed pad AMF-106)
concepts.force_note: isotropic: it cannot tell writing from tremor, so it resists both
concepts.bandwidth: solenoid 5-20 ms (ASSUMPTION); SQUIGGLE 7 mm/s is too slow to modulate at tremor rates
concepts.size: ball d 2 mm: heel contact radius >= 7.6 mm plus the brake
concepts.heat: coil heat near the fingers if held on
concepts.roll: roll-invariant ball, contact as the ball
concepts.verdict: Tremor damping only; weak for guidance; roll-invariant
concepts.labels: CALC; LIT HAP-68; MFR AMF-106, AMF-108

concepts.name: Controllable friction pads
concepts.principle: Electroadhesion pulls the paper to a heel pad; or ultrasonic vibration lowers the pad's friction; or a steered anisotropic (scale-like) pad
concepts.actuators: high-voltage electrode pad; or a piezo pad; or a pad on a steering motor
concepts.force_note: a 24 mm2 pad at 1-5 kPa on paper adds 0.024-0.120 N of normal force (dielectric targets: pre-contact pressure 1-100 x below release, AMF-114); ultrasonic squeeze films need a smooth, airtight contact (AMF-115; paper is porous); anisotropic pads (AMF-116) slide with 3-6 x the drag of a rolling wheel (ASSUMPTION ratio)
concepts.verdict: Reject: too weak (EA), unlikely on paper (ultrasonic), draggy (anisotropic)

concepts.name: Others considered
concepts.principle: (a) piezo 'walking' foot with the paper as the slider; (b) 4 mm brushless hub (Orbray BMN04) driving the wheel directly; (c) asymmetric-vibration pseudo-force (study K); (d) desk board
concepts.force_any_dir_N: (b) 0.40 N continuous at r 1.5 mm with an assumed 100:1 head
concepts.force_note: (a) paper compliance absorbs the micrometre vibration (ASSUMPTION); (b) too weak and slow: 73 mm/s no-load; (c) no net force; (d) 0.4 N cap, grounded, separate device
concepts.verdict: Keep the board for practice at a desk; the others are not pursued
